# About This Book {#sec-index-about .unnumbered}

```{r}
#| label: setup-index
#| include: false
front_tbl <- function(id) readRDS(file.path("..", "tables", paste0(id, ".rds")))
front_build <- front_tbl("T-build-report")
front_tiers <- front_tbl("T-bib-tiers")
front_verifiers <- front_tbl("T-verifiers")
front_assets <- read.csv(file.path("..", "refs", "asset-index.csv"),
                         stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
front_value <- function(q) front_build$Value[front_build$Quantity == q]
front_tier <- function(q) front_tiers$Entries[front_tiers$Tier == q]
front_n_pdf <- sum(front_assets$pdf %in% TRUE)
front_n_ocr <- sum(front_assets$ocr %in% TRUE)
```

This is the theory-and-literature companion to *Targeting Toward Inferential Goals in
Bayesian Item Response Models for Estimating Person-Specific Latent Traits*. The
manuscript was submitted under a Rasch-only title; its revision extends selected
questions to the two-parameter model, and the title here follows that broader umbrella.
The umbrella is **Rasch-centred**, not a claim of parallel depth across the two models:
Parts I--VII form the theory spine, and Part VIII is a focused 2PL extension
of the mechanisms for which free discriminations materially change the argument. The
book sets out the mathematics that paper rests on, traces each result to the work that
established it, and says plainly where the paper's own statements need correcting.

Four documents divide the work, and it helps to know which is authority for what.

| | Question it answers | Authority for |
|---|---|---|
| **This book** | What is the mathematics, and who established it? | Definitions, classical results, identification, the literature genealogy, decision-theoretic justifications |
| The simulation volume [@lee_simulation_2026] | What did we run, and what did it show? | The design grid, realized values, Monte Carlo error, gate verdicts, results |
| The case-study volume [@lee_casestudy_2026] | What changes on real tests? | Thirteen Item Response Warehouse cases, both item models, consequence and transfer — with no correctness claims of its own |
| The manuscript | What is the contribution? | The paper's claims, and nothing else |

Around these sit the software the models are fitted with — `DPMirt`
[@lee_dpmirt_2026], `DPprior` [@lee_dpprior_2026], and `IRTsimrel`
[@lee_irtsimrel_2026] — the two methods papers the packages implement
[@lee_reliability-targeted_2026; @lee_design-conditional_2026], and two corpus
studies of the Item Response Warehouse that measure what real tests look like: one
of reliability across 889 datasets [@lee_reliability-distribution_2026] and one of
latent-distribution shape across 504 [@lee_theta-nonnormality_2026]. Where a chapter
leans on any of them, it says so in its provenance section.

The book has three evidence zones, not a blanket simulation-independence rule.

| Zone | Role | Boundary rule |
|---|---|---|
| **Parts I--VII** | Rasch-centred theory spine | Definitions, mechanisms, sourced results, and derivations lead. A realized companion result may enter only as a registered, explicitly attributed inset; it does not become a premise of the theory. |
| **Part VIII** | Focused 2PL extension | Develops the information, reliability, and identification changes created by free discriminations. Its realized simulation and case-study passages are explicitly labelled empirical insets and remain bounded by their source designs. |
| **Part IX** | Evidence synthesis | Reads the companion volumes' realized results back into the theory. Frozen-source assertions and confirmatory/exploratory labels govern every imported result. |

This zoning admits the empirical crossings that are already useful in earlier chapters
without pretending that Parts I--VIII would stand unchanged if the studies had never
been run. The cross-book register records each crossing and the claim boundary it must
keep.

## Who this is for, and three ways in

**A practitioner** deciding how to score a short test: @sec-ch01 for the problem,
@sec-ch08 for what reliability means and which coefficient answers which question,
@sec-ch17 for why one set of scores cannot serve every purpose, @sec-ch20 for ranking
and cut-scores, @sec-ch25 for what changes when items are allowed to differ in
discrimination, and @sec-ch27 and @sec-ch28 for what the simulation and the real-test
corpus actually found.

**A methodologist** assessing the work: Parts II through VI in order, followed by the
focused 2PL sensitivity route in Part VIII (@sec-ch24 through @sec-ch26). The claim-level
index in @sec-appendix-a distinguishes `proved-here`, `partial-derivation`, and
`source-only`; nothing is asserted without an argument or a source locator.

**A reviewer checking a specific point**: @sec-appendix-c lists every place the
submitted manuscript is wrong, imprecise, or merely unclear, with the section that
fixes it.

## How to read a numbered result

Every definition, theorem, proposition, lemma, and corollary carries a provenance tag:

> **Theorem 8.3** (Jensen gap) · *restated from* Lee (2026, Prop. 2)

*Restated* — established in the cited source, reproduced here, possibly in different
notation. *Adapted* — established there for a different setting, modified here, with the
modification stated. *Derived here; no originality claim* — proved in this text without
claiming that the result is new to the literature.

An explicit novelty or priority claim would require a separate prior-art search. None of
the current `derived-here` tags makes such a claim.

Restated and adapted numbered results carry a page-, section-, equation-, or
theorem-level locator, and V1 requires a locator-read source for every one of them.
Independent literature is `primary-read`; this programme's own directly inspected books,
manuscripts, packages, code, and tables are `programme-artifact-read`. The latter tier
establishes fidelity to the named artifact, not independent corroboration.

**Narrative citations are held to a weaker standard, and the tier says which is which.**
A source tagged `primary-held` was available but has not been read at a locator for this
book. Such a source may be named in the text — to point at a literature or credit a
lineage — but it carries no numbered result and no equation-level attribution.
**The gap is disclosed, not hidden**, and @sec-appendix-d separately annotates
`r front_tier("primary-read")` independent reads and
`r front_tier("programme-artifact-read")` programme-artifact reads.

## What the sources are, and what they are not

The recursive source inventory spans nine reference libraries: `r front_n_pdf` PDFs and
`r front_n_ocr` Markdown sidecars representing `r nrow(front_assets)` indexed assets. The
bibliography contains `r front_value("Bibliography entries")` entries:
`r front_tier("primary-read")` `primary-read`,
`r front_tier("programme-artifact-read")` `programme-artifact-read`, `r front_tier("primary-held")`
`primary-held`, and `r front_tier("secondary")` `secondary`.

Parts II through IV were seeded by six appendix drafts written during the manuscript's
first revision. Those drafts were machine-generated by four different models and never
reconciled with one another. **They carry no citation authority here.** Every statement
taken from them has been re-derived or re-verified against the source named in the
chapter's provenance section, and the audit that established which of their claims were
unsourced — 64 of 106 numbered results under the corrected paired-block audit — is
recorded in the build log. Saying this is
not modesty; it is the same standard the book applies to everything else it cites.

## Reproducing this book

```bash
Rscript code/R/14-build-all.R
```

This command harvests and validates the bibliography, regenerates tables and figures,
renders the book, and runs `r nrow(front_verifiers)` verifiers (V1–V9) together with
`r front_value("Claim-level checkers (beyond V1--V9)")` claim-level checkers, including
`r front_value("Numerical checks (V8)")` numerical checks in V8. Chapters read only frozen
tables under `tables/` and figures under `book/figures/`. They compute nothing.

**What that machinery does and does not guarantee is worth stating exactly, because
an earlier edition of this page overstated it.** Every table and figure is generated by
a script in `code/R/` and regenerated on every build, so a displayed artifact cannot
drift from the code that made it. Prose, however, is written by hand. Where a sentence
in Part IX quotes a companion volume, the binding is not the rendering pipeline but
`manifest/evidence-claim-register.csv`, which records
`r front_value("Audited evidence claims")` imported claims with their chapter, line,
source edition, snapshot locator and field.
`r front_value("  of which independently recomputed")` of those are recomputed from the
frozen store at build time and fail the build on divergence; the rest are registered
for audit without being executed. @sec-appg-claim-checks gives the full contract. The
discipline exists because a hand-copied number goes stale silently, and this project has
been bitten by exactly that — including once in the edition before this one.

The registers that make the provenance checkable are under `manifest/`: every numbered
result, every notation symbol, every declared restatement from the companion volume,
every reviewer comment and the section that answers it, and the running list of
corrections to the manuscript.
